transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM); Asha Verma (CTO, Zenith), Tom Hastings (Head Cloud Infra), Priya Shah (Lead ML Eng)

Summary (auto):
Initial POC kickoff to scope private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region locking, and egress constraints. Define success criteria (latency, throughput, data residency), workload sizing and benchmark plan, and timeline for a 3-week pilot. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics:
- PrivateLink vs VPC peering tradeoffs
- Region residency and availability zones
- Egress/egress-blocking and allowed egress endpoints
- Baseline benchmarks (model size, qps, sequence lengths)
- POC success criteria and timeline

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? We'll do a short agenda: network options, residency, benchmarks, success criteria and timeline. Marcus, want to lead network?
[00:18] Marcus Nguyen: Yeah sure. Hi Tom, hi Asha, Priya. I'll start with the two common private networking approaches we see: VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. High level, peering is simple, lower ops but can cross region routing complications; PrivateLink gives you endpoint-level control and egress minimization.
[00:40] Tom Hastings: Quick clarification — our security team is nervous about any internet egress. They want everything to stay in our VPC and only reach Redwood endpoints over private connectivity.
[00:52] Marcus Nguyen: Totally understood. We can support both patterns — PrivateLink is often the best fit for strict egress controls because the traffic never traverses a public IP. Peering can also work but you need to lock down route tables and NAT behavior.
[01:10] Asha Verma: Also region question — legal requires EU resident data not leave eu-west-1. So can Redwood pin inference to eu-west-1?
[01:22] Lena Park: Yes, we support region pinning for private deployments. For hosted, we can route to eu-west-1 instances and enforce residency for the POC. For Dedicated/Private, you can run the control plane in your VPC or our private control plane options.
[01:40] Priya Shah: For the POC, our workload is a classification pipeline where we send batches of clinical notes. Typical request size is 1–2 KB, tokenized into ~200 tokens average. We expect burst to 150 qps, sustained around 40 qps. Models: we want to try a 13B LLM initially, possibly 70B later.
[02:05] Marcus Nguyen: Great, that's helpful. For 13B with sequence lengths ~200, we usually recommend starting with batch size of 4 and target latency SLO of 200 ms p50 for gen calls, 95th below 600 ms — but with private networking the extra hop can add 10–40ms depending on routing.
[02:23] Tom Hastings: Is caching an option? We have a lot of repeated prefixes in our workload.
[02:30] Marcus Nguyen: Yes, Redwood supports prefix and KV cache to lower token compute and reduce cold-start costs. For repeated prefixes you'd see big wins — we'll instrument that in benchmarks.
[02:50] Lena Park: On the POC success criteria we usually capture: 1) Latency targets, 2) Cost per 1k requests, 3) No data exfiltration — all traffic stays within pinned region and private links, 4) Integration sanity — SSO, audit logs, KMS. Any additions?
[03:15] Asha Verma: Also need to validate logging retention and that audit logs can be forwarded to our SIEM, Splunk Cloud — no logs to third-party unless encrypted and stored in our account.
[03:30] Diego Ramos: We can forward audit logs to your account. For Private deployment we can also ship logs directly to an S3 bucket in your account with SSE-KMS. I'll follow up with the exact config.
[03:50] Priya Shah: For the benchmark, what's a realistic test harness? We can send a replay of 24 hours of traffic at 4x speed to simulate burst.
[04:05] Marcus Nguyen: That works. For POC we typically run: baseline single-client latencies, multi-client sustained qps for 30–60 minutes, cold-start scenarios, and caching enabled vs disabled. We'll need sample payloads and a script.
[04:25] Tom Hastings: Regarding network — we use strict NACLs and do port restriction. If we do PrivateLink, do we need special SGs?
[04:34] Marcus Nguyen: You'll create an endpoint ENI in your subnet; SG rules will control ingress. We can share a templated security group and sample route table entries. Also note PrivateLink supports inter-region via interface endpoints in each region, but cross-region replication isn't automatic — region pinning is explicit.
[04:55] Asha Verma: What about HIPAA-ish requirements? We don't want PHI anywhere unencrypted at rest.
[05:03] Diego Ramos: For Private/ Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). At-rest data volumes and caches are encrypted, and we can provide attestation docs. I'll add SOC2 + HIPAA guidance in the follow-up.
[05:20] Priya Shah: For the initial benchmark, we'd like to measure p50/p95/p99 and tail latency impact when we increase seq len to 512 and move to batching of 8.
[05:32] Marcus Nguyen: Noted. That will stress the KV cache and memory pressure. For 13B at 512 tokens with batch 8 you should expect much higher latencies — we'll quantify. Also quantization and compiled kernels can improve perf; we can recommend quant profiles for the POC.
[06:00] Lena Park: Timeline callout: We'd like to keep the pilot to three weeks after network connectivity is established. Proposed schedule: week 0 — network & IAM setup; week 1 — baseline benchmarks and integration; week 2 — stability/scale and run guardrail tests; week 3 — findings and decision. Thoughts?
[06:25] Asha Verma: Sounds good. How long to get PrivateLink up? Our infra team usually needs ~3 business days for endpoint approvals.
[06:35] Marcus Nguyen: If you can open a ticket with the support template we'll provide, we can help speed it. We'll also provide CloudFormation snippets for the interface endpoint and SGs which typically reduces the back-and-forth.
[06:50] Tom Hastings: Egress constraints: we completely block outbound internet but allow connections to our partner endpoints. Will Redwood require any public egress for control plane access?
[07:04] Marcus Nguyen: If you use our Private deployment with a customer-managed control plane in your VPC, no public egress is required. For Redwood Hosted via PrivateLink, there are outbound connections to Redwood-managed endpoints but they stay on AWS network private addresses. We will enumerate the exact CIDR/endpoint list.
[07:28] Priya Shah: For data residency, if we pin to eu-west-1, does the KV cache ever replicate to us-east?
[07:36] Marcus Nguyen: No, for pinned deployments we maintain KV and persistent state in the pinned region. Cross-region fallback is an optional policy we'll only enable if you permit it. For POC we can keep it strict in eu-west-1.
[07:52] Lena Park: Actionable items so far: Marcus diagrams, Diego compliance docs, Priya workload samples. We'll get a draft benchmark plan by next week.
[08:05] Asha Verma: One more thing — network capture for compliance. Our audit team will want to see a packet capture showing private connectivity and no public egress. Is that feasible?
[08:18] Marcus Nguyen: Yes, we can provide traffic flow diagrams and guidance on how to capture on your side. We don't provide pcaps ourselves but we'll provide sample tcpdump commands and expected flow.
[08:30] Tom Hastings: About cost — can you ballpark cost for the pilot? Even rough numbers per 1k calls would help budget approval.
[08:40] Lena Park: We'll run a baseline cost estimate once we have exact qps and model choice. For a 13B model with our usual batching and caching, ballpark numbers are X tokens per second... (inaudible) we'll capture that in the spreadsheet.
[08:58] Priya Shah: Ok sending sample logs and sample payloads by Thursday.
[09:03] Diego Ramos: Noted, I'll track that.
[09:10] Marcus Nguyen: Quick technical aside — if you plan to use our Dedicated racks in your cloud region, we'd want to size GPUs based on peak concurrency. For 150 qps bursts with 13B, that likely maps to 2–3 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on batching and KV hit rate. We'll include sizing options in the benchmark doc.
[09:35] Priya Shah: Are there any known issues with SMIME or corporate proxies? Our environment uses an outbound proxy for some control plane interactions.
[09:45] Marcus Nguyen: For PrivateLink/pinned deployments proxies are usually a non-issue because traffic is private. If you must use a proxy, we need to test the control-plane handshake; we'll add a proxy test to the checklist.
[10:05] Asha Verma: SLA — for Dedicated we will need daytime uptime and an SLO for tail latencies. Can that be part of the POC?
[10:16] Lena Park: We can definitely capture SLO baselines during the POC and propose SLOs for Dedicated contract stage.
[10:25] Tom Hastings: Ok, can we talk quick about identity — SSO? We need RBAC and SCIM provisioning for team members.
[10:32] Diego Ramos: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. For private deployments we can integrate with your IdP directly. I'll share the SAML metadata examples.
[10:45] Priya Shah: For the benchmark harness — do you support client-side instrumentation like open telemetry?
[10:51] Marcus Nguyen: Yes, we expose request-level metrics and traces; we can provide an OTLP exporter template and sample dashboards.
[11:05] Asha Verma: On the legal side — data processing agreement, can you provide the DPIA template?
[11:12] Lena Park: We'll surface the DPA and DPIA templates. Diego will include them in the follow-up packet.
[11:25] Marcus Nguyen: A couple of gotchas: if you route via peering and have transitive routes, watch out for inter-AZ charges if traffic crosses AZ boundaries; also ensure your MTU isn't modified in the path — we've seen fragmentation causing higher latency.
[11:45] Tom Hastings: Good note. We'll keep AZs aligned.
[12:00] Priya Shah: For the formal success criteria, can we write them now?
[12:05] Lena Park: Sure — draft: (1) Residency: 100% requests and state remain in eu-west-1; (2) Latency: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 700ms for 13B typical seq lengths; (3) Throughput: sustain 40 qps for 60 minutes with bursts to 150 qps without errors; (4) Security: PrivateLink or Private deployment with customer KMS and audit log forwarding; (5) Integration: SSO and trace export working; (6) Cost: cost per 1k requests within agreed budget — define post-baseline.
[12:30] Asha Verma: Those look good. Add: no third-party access to plaintext payloads.
[12:35] Diego Ramos: We'll include language in the POC scoping doc.
[12:45] Marcus Nguyen: Ok I'll outline the benchmark plan: test matrix will include small (200 tokens), medium (512), and large (1k) sequences across batch sizes 1,4,8; caching on/off; sustained run at target qps; and failure injection (network loss) to test graceful degradation.
[13:10] Priya Shah: What's the expected turnaround to get the baseline numbers?
[13:18] Marcus Nguyen: If we get network up within a week, we can run an initial baseline within 3 business days and share a spreadsheet.
[13:30] Lena Park: Anything else missing?
[13:34] Tom Hastings: One operational ask — can we have a kill-switch? If unusual traffic detected, our infra needs an API to cut connectivity quickly.
[13:43] Marcus Nguyen: Yes, we can add a fail-closed hook and show you runbooks.
[13:50] Asha Verma: Ok if we get those docs and the network template today/tomorrow we can start provisioning.
[13:57] Diego Ramos: I'll drop the compliance pack and the SOC2 links after the call.
[14:05] Lena Park: Great. Quick recap and next steps: Marcus will share PrivateLink & peering diagrams and a baseline benchmark plan; Diego will send compliance docs and SAML/SCIM examples; Priya will send workload samples; Redwood to run baseline benchmarks and share cost/latency spreadsheet. We'll schedule the follow-up checkpoint for ~2025-07-22.
[14:30] Asha Verma: Thanks everyone. End of call.
